correctness.rationale: Formal inversion with T=1+2A yields F ≡ -A-A²-2A³+2A⁴ modulo four. Classical norm-Euclidean factorization proves r_{-4}=4 C4 and r_{-8}=2 C8 for all positive indices including ramified primes. Removing precisely axial solutions and applying Frobenius modulo two gives the three square-correction terms; odd-squarefree factorization yields the prime detection criterion. Independent marked-overpartition dynamic programming, theta expansion, direct norm counts, and all-index residues agree through n=420. No finite experiment is used to conclude an infinite identity.

value.rationale: Determines a precise natural invariant — the modulo-four signed overlined-part statistic — for every positive index in terms of multiplicative divisor characters and a small finite set of theta-square corrections. On odd squarefree inputs, residue 2 is exactly a primality-plus-modulo-eight signal while all composites vanish, a meaningful structural classification not an arbitrary slice or finite-table recomputation. It gives a number-theoretic evaluation method that does not enumerate overpartitions.
